items.title: The agency-to-merchant shift moves most money flow through Booking's own books
items.summary: Merchant revenues grew 25.5% to $17,755M in 2025 while agency revenues fell 6.5% to $7,968M; 70% of group gross bookings were on a merchant basis in 2025, up from 63% in 2024.
items.implication: Subledger, revenue recognition, payments-to-ledger and payout capacity must scale with merchant volume rather than with agency invoicing; architecture investment should follow the money flow.

items.title: Traveler cash held before stay is a large, growing liability
items.summary: Deferred merchant bookings rose to $5,270M at 31 December 2025 from $4,031M, described as cash received from travelers before the company completes its performance obligations and mostly refundable on cancellation.
items.implication: A dedicated traveler-funds and deferred-bookings ledger with daily reconciliation to cash and safeguarding positions is a control-critical capability, not a reporting afterthought.

items.title: Payment facilitation is now a revenue line with its own cost base
items.summary: Merchant revenue includes payment facilitation revenue such as card processing rebates and customer processing fees; revenue as a share of gross bookings rose partly from facilitating payments, while merchant transaction costs rose by $381M.
items.implication: Payment fees, rebates and PSP costs must be captured at transaction level and reconciled, so finance can show the margin of the payments business and validate PSP fees.

items.title: Licensed e-money entities add regulatory reporting to the finance core
items.summary: Booking Holdings Financial Services consists of licensed and regulated e-money institutions supporting the brands' payment products; its Irish arm holds a Central Bank of Ireland e-money licence and intended to start trading as an EMI in 2025. The 10-K notes that subsidiaries providing payment services are subject to licensing.
items.implication: Safeguarding, capital and regulatory returns for each licensed entity must be produced from the same ledger and payment data, with entity-level segregation in the chart of accounts.

items.title: PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation are named risks to EU payment features
items.summary: The 2025 10-K names the EU's Payment Services Directive 3 and proposed Payment Services Regulation as regulatory risks to payment features offered in the EU.
items.implication: Payment and settlement contracts into finance should be versioned and decoupled from PSP specifics so regulatory changes are absorbed in adapters, not in the ledger.

items.title: Booking.com's SAP core has been on a long S/4HANA path via Central Finance
items.summary: Booking.com job postings state that the SAP environment runs on HANA, moved to Simple Finance in February 2016 and began the S/4HANA journey in 2019 with Central Finance; FI-CA and BRIM are in the stack and the Financial Systems team owns SAP, HANA and connected third-party systems.
items.implication: Target-state decisions must sequence Central Finance, the high-volume subledger and brand ledgers explicitly; the multi-year migration is the backbone of the architecture roadmap.

items.title: The Transformation Program explicitly targets processes, systems and procurement
items.summary: The Transformation Program covers modernizing processes and systems, workforce reduction, procurement optimization and real estate; it delivered about $250M savings in 2025 and had enabled about $550M annual run-rate savings by year end, with $205M transformation costs in 2025.
items.implication: Finance-systems architecture decisions are judged on run-rate savings and cost-to-serve; the portfolio must show ROI per programme and avoid trading savings for control risk.

items.title: ICFR is effective and audited — the bar is to keep it that way through change
items.summary: Management concluded internal control over financial reporting was effective at 31 December 2025 and Deloitte & Touche LLP attested to it, with no material change in the fourth quarter.
items.implication: Every migration and brand convergence step needs explicit control impact assessment; architecture governance is part of the SOX change-management control environment.

items.title: Indirect tax and digital services taxes create material, jurisdiction-specific exposure
items.summary: The 10-K reports a $337M 2024 accrual for Italian indirect tax matters and $89M of 2025 expense for other indirect tax matters; digital services taxes range from 1.5% to 10% of in-jurisdiction revenue, and the EU 'VAT in the digital age' proposal is named as a source of added complexity.
items.implication: Tax determination must be rule-driven at transaction level with an auditable record per booking, so new regimes are configured rather than coded per brand.

items.title: EUR and GBP exposure makes FX accounting and hedging a daily concern
items.summary: Principal foreign currency exposures are the euro and British pound; the company uses derivatives to limit FX impacts, and FX added about 3 points to 2025 revenue growth.
items.implication: Cash positions and FX exposure must be visible daily per entity and currency from payments, payouts and bank data to drive hedging and revaluation.

items.title: Multiple brands with different models must converge on one finance core
items.summary: Booking Holdings runs Booking.com (Netherlands), Priceline (US), Agoda (Singapore), KAYAK and OpenTable with distinct business models; the architecture role description assigns final decision rights on converging disparate financial technologies into a unified global platform.
items.implication: Convergence needs a canonical finance contract and adapter kit plus clear decision rights; mandating a big-bang migration across brands would stall delivery.

items.title: Decision velocity and target-state clarity are the stated outcomes for architecture
items.summary: The role's objectives are to strengthen architecture governance and decision velocity, improve target-state quality, reduce ambiguity and unresolved dependencies on complex initiatives, and move from tactical workarounds to scalable designs without compromising controls.
items.implication: Decision lead time, decision durability and conformance rates are the measurable outcomes the architecture products must move.

items.title: Local payment methods expand the settlement and reconciliation surface
items.summary: Booking.com partnered with Antom (Ant International) in January 2025 to add local payment options across Asian markets.
items.implication: Each new APM brings new settlement formats, currencies and fee structures; payments-to-ledger needs pattern-based onboarding to keep launch times short.

items.title: Close, reconciliation and planning tooling around SAP is assumed, not confirmed
items.summary: A third-party job listing (not verified on Booking's careers site) mentions subledger-to-GL reconciliation, revenue recognition, FinDB, BlackLine, OneStream and SAP RISE in Booking Holdings' finance landscape.
items.implication: The model treats BlackLine, OneStream, FinDB and RISE as assumptions; decisions depending on them should be validated before use.
